title: Pip's Listening Walk
checkpoint: Phase 1 (Introduction) — environmental sounds and voice sounds. Read this one ALOUD to the children.
note_for_grown_ups: An Introduction-phase book — there are no sounds to decode yet, so YOU read it and the children join in. Pause at every 'join in' line and let them make the sound with you. Ask 'what made that sound?' before you turn the page.

pages.text: Pip woke up early. The garden was full of sounds, and Pip wanted to find every single one.
pages.join_in: Cup your hands behind your ears — big listening ears!
pages.illustration: Wide garden dawn scene. Pip the sand-brown sparrow with a tufted head sits on the edge of the ivy nest above the shed, head cocked, one wing raised. Soft gold morning light, long shadows. Sound is suggested by faint pale ripples in the air, not by symbols.

pages.text: First he heard the gate. It did not squeak quietly. It squeaked all the way up, like a question.
pages.join_in: Eeee-eek! Make the gate squeak — start low and go high.
pages.illustration: Close view of a weathered wooden garden gate swinging on a rusty hinge, Pip perched on the top bar bobbing with the movement. The hinge is drawn in detail — flaking paint, a bright worn spot. Pip's eyes are wide and delighted.

pages.text: Then he heard rain on the shed roof. Not big rain. Little rain, tapping like tiny feet.
pages.join_in: Tap your fingertips on your knees — quiet, quick, all together.
pages.illustration: Corrugated shed roof from just above, fine drizzle bouncing off it in small bright dots. Pip shelters under the guttering, dry, watching. Cool grey-green palette so it contrasts with the gold of page one.

pages.text: Under the hedge something went snuffle, snuffle, snuffle. Pip did not know that sound at all.
pages.join_in: Snuffle, snuffle! Breathe in through your nose like a hungry hedgehog.
pages.illustration: Dark leafy hedge bottom, only a wet black nose and two bright eyes visible in the shadows. Pip peers in from outside, tail up, curious and a tiny bit unsure. Half the page is dark leaf shapes.

pages.text: Out came Moss, with a leaf stuck to his nose. "That was ME," he said. "That is my breakfast sound."
pages.join_in: Say it in Moss's shy little voice: "That was me."
pages.illustration: Moss the berry-coloured hedgehog steps out of the hedge blinking, a single yellow leaf balanced on his snout, spikes flecked with dew. Pip hops back in surprise, wings half open. Warm and funny, not frightening.

pages.text: High in the old oak, Olive gave one long hoot. Every bird in the garden stopped to listen.
pages.join_in: Hoo-hoo! One long hoot, then wait — can you hear the quiet after it?
pages.illustration: Looking up the trunk of the old oak. Olive the plum-coloured owl on a branch far above, round and spotted, beak open mid-hoot. The whole garden below her drawn small and still. Emphasise the silence with lots of empty sky.

pages.text: Pip flew home for tea. He shut his eyes and counted every sound he had found. There were seven.
pages.join_in: Shut your eyes. How many sounds can YOU hear right now?
pages.illustration: Pip curled in the twiggy ivy nest with his eyes shut and a contented expression, evening light going pink behind him. Around the edge of the page, faint ghosted outlines of the gate, the rain, Moss and Olive — the sounds he is remembering.
